ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The image shows a large gray cube, with the outer surface painted gray; the visible front face, top face, and side face are all divided by grid lines into 3 segments along each edge, so the whole is 3×3×3 small cubes. Reasoning: The large cube has side length 3 cm, and the small cubes have side length 1 cm, so there are 3 small cubes along each edge. The small cubes with exactly 2 faces painted are located on the edges of the large cube but not at the vertices. A cube has 12 edges; in the 3×3×3 case, after removing the two corner blocks from each edge, only 1 small cube remains in the middle. Therefore the number is 12×1=12.

method.method_draft: Use the edge-position counting rule. From the text, note the large cube is 3 cm on each side and is cut into 1 cm cubes, so it forms a 3 by 3 by 3 array. From the image, confirm the cube is subdivided into 3 smaller cubes along each visible edge and all outside faces are painted. A small cube has exactly 2 painted faces precisely when it lies on an edge of the large cube but is not a corner cube. A cube has 12 edges, and for a 3-by-3-by-3 cube each edge has exactly one non-corner small cube in the middle. Therefore the count is 12 × 1 = 12.
